correctness.rationale: For any torsion abelian G and finitely supported a, take finite subgroup H carrying a. Fourier primitive idempotents e_chi of norm one decompose entire l1(G) into finitely many annihilating corners. Every corner has dense invertible elements: approximate an arbitrary corner element by one supported on a finite larger subgroup K, use the finite product-of-fields Fourier decomposition, then shift a tiny scalar away from finitely many roots. For arbitrary b (possibly infinite support), choose near b_chi invertible v_chi in corners where Fourier a coefficient vanishes, and otherwise use the nonzero scalar alpha_chi. The two-case explicit formulas produce x*y=a*b+h for arbitrary h of small l1 norm, with ||x-a||<epsilon/4 and ||y-b||<epsilon/2. Thus every target ball is covered; no finite example substitutes for arbitrary-group argument.

value.rationale: A natural structural boundary in the outstanding torsion-abelian convolution openness problem: no locally nonopen pair can contain even one finitely supported factor, including when the other is infinitely supported. Stronger than an already known all-finite local aperture calculation.

limitations: Requires at least one finitely supported input. Makes no claim for two infinite-support factors/global openness, and no new aperture dichotomy for two finite inputs.
